title: [leyden-dev] Announcement: renaming current `premain` branch to `premain-old` and creating new `premain`
content:
Thread: Announcement: renaming current `premain` branch to `premain-old` and creating new `premain`
List: leyden-dev@openjdk.org | Messages: 1+

[OP] Hi, During last Leyden meeting there was proposal to rename old `premain` branch and create new `premain` branch based on current mainline JDK. The only major project left in current `premain` branch is AOT code caching. But the current PR [1] is based on mainline JDK already and not `premain`. Merging mainline changes into leyden:premain become very complex. As result the branch was not updated in 2 months. Current `premain` branch contains experimental changes we collected for the past 3 years. Not all of them will be pushed into mainline. And we don't want to clean them up to match state of mainline JDK. It will be waste of our time and some changes could be useful in a future. We propose to rename current `premain` to `premain-old` to keep history and our experiments. And create new `premain` branch from `leyden:master` which is in sync with mainline JDK. I will push AOT code caching changes from PR to new `premain` and we may "cherry-pick` some changes from `premain-old`. This will simply merges from mainline (Valhalla when it lands in mainline) and our internal testing will continue run without need to change configuration. Please let me know other alternatives to these changes (like keeping current `premain` and creating `premain-new`, for example). Note, there will be separate e-mail after renaming is done with instructions to update your fork [2]. And for those who directly work with `premain` branch [3]. I listed instructions at the bottom. Please verify if they are

title: Liquid Glass, Material 3, and a Lot of Plumbing
content:
It has been one of those weeks where the diff is bigger than the headline. The headline is short — Codename One now ships modern native themes: an iOS "liquid glass" look and an Android Material 3 look, bundled into the iOS and Android ports, on by default in the Playground, and selectable from a brand new menu in the simulator. The diff behind that headline is several thousand lines across the platform ports, the simulator, the GUI plumbing, and a small army of screenshot tests.

What is Codename One? Codename One is an open-source framework for building native iOS, Android, desktop, and web apps from a single Java or Kotlin codebase. Learn more at codenameone.com.

The theme behind the work is simple: Codename One should look modern out of the box on every platform we ship to, and it should feel fast. Almost everything in the past week of commits is in service of one of those two goals.
author: Shai Almog
